doc.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Early piano, family support and moving to Queens
summary: He recalls early musical signs, singing as a toddler, and starting piano lessons after the family moves to Queens.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me take you back for a minute, what led you to the piano, and was your family supportive of your music?
Okay. I just recently got a story from my mother. She said — it’s funny — she said when I was in my crib, you know the bar that would be on the crib, I’d be going like this—

She swears I was doing like this when I was a baby in the crib, just going like this, so she realized I had some musical talent. And I remember when I was three years old, this I remember, when I was three years old I would walk around the room singing “Oh My Papa,” by Eddie Fisher.

Yeah. Somehow I knew every word to that tune at three. Three years old. Now a three year old, you can imagine, a three year old singing an Italian song in Harlem you know. So anyway, we moved from Harlem it was like ’57, we moved from Harlem to Queens. And it’s funny because I felt like at seven years old I picked the house. And it turned out that there was a piano teacher right in that neighborhood that I could walk to her house from my house. They didn’t know this. And the church, she was an organist, it was right down the block also. Everything walking distance. So we went to her house and I began piano lessons. And she also was very instrumental in my developing my composing © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-
